corrections.form_value: 'with no AI' (summary); 'The idea was written before any feedback and without AI' (what_was_assigned); 'on an idea already written without AI' (reason)
corrections.source_says: The paper never says whether students could use AI while ideating. It says only that each student developed an idea in Round 01 (Crazy 8s, then a 15-minute refinement) and submitted it for feedback. The only AI role it describes is the Round 02 feedback. Write 'written in Round 01, before any feedback (AI use during ideation not stated)'. Eligibility does not change.
corrections.quote: In Round 01, each student developed a startup idea to mitigate academic stress using the ‘Crazy 8s’ ... The ideation outcomes were then submitted for feedback.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 431), Section 3.1, Round 01 and Round 02 paragraphs

corrections.form_value: '5-point Likert surveys' (summary); 'on a 5-point Likert scale' (S1-O1); 'Four survey questions on a 5-point Likert scale (H2)' (S1-O2); 'Six survey questions on a 5-point Likert scale (H3)' (S1-O3)
corrections.source_says: The paper states a 5-point scale only for the four H1 items (positivity, supportiveness, fairness, competence) and for the H4 structure items. The H2 and H3 paragraphs give no scale. Section 3.4 says the survey also had three-point items (1 negative, 2 neutral, 3 positive). In Figure 3 every 'overall' item, which all three outcome names include, spans only 1 to 3. The paper does not say which items were three-point, so the strings should not call every item 5-point.
corrections.quote: Likert-scale responses ranged from 1 (“strongly disagree”) to 5 (“strongly agree”). Three-point scale responses included 1 (negative), 2 (neutral), and 3 (positive).
corrections.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 433), Section 3.4 and Section 4 H1; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 434), H2, H3, and H4 paragraphs and the 'overall' boxes in Figure 3

corrections.form_value: Twenty-five design-related students from four Bavarian universities
corrections.source_says: The paper does not call the students design-related. They came from 'a variety of academic programs', including computer science, mechanical engineering, and business administration, and were expected to be familiar with ideation. The paper's 'design-related field' wording applies to the lecturers. Write 'Twenty-five students from four Bavarian universities'.
corrections.quote: The students represented a variety of academic programs, including human factors engineering, architecture, computer science, human-computer interaction, design leadership, industrial design, mechanical engineering, and business administration.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 432), Section 3.3 Participant recruitment

corrections.form_value: Figure 1 caption: 'Following a within-subjects design, each student received two anonymized feedback comments'
corrections.source_says: The quoted sentence is an annotation inside the Figure 1 graphic, under the 'Core experiment' bracket. The caption reads 'Figure 1. Overview of study design'. The locator should read 'Figure 1, annotation under Core experiment'.
corrections.quote: Following a within-subjects design, each student received two anonymized feedback comments—one from GPT-4 and one from a lecturer—in a single document.

confirmed: Version matches the PDF: version of record, Proceedings of the Design Society 5 (ICED25), pp. 429-438, doi 10.1017/pds.2025.10057, 'Published online by Cambridge University Press'. The PDF has 10 pages, and I read all 10 (PDF p. 1 header, page footers).

Title and the three authors match (PDF p. 1). The paper mentions no supplement, preregistration, data or code link, funding, or company role, so the supplement, preregistered, data_and_code, and company_involvement values fit (PDF pp. 1-10).

Within-subjects design: each student received two anonymized comments, one from GPT-4 and one from a lecturer, in a single document. The order was randomized, 13 human first and 12 AI first. The assignment quote is verbatim, 28 words (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1 and Figure 1).

has_randomized_people_study is false. Only the reading order of the two comments was randomized. The core experiment has three stages (ideation, feedback, assessment of the feedback) and no revision round, and no idea was scored. The abstract's 'facilitates iterative idea refinement' rests on no scored revision (PDF p. 1; p. 3, Section 3.1 and Figure 1).

design_class 'other' and context_class 'none' fit. Students rated GPT-4 feedback and lecturer feedback on their own idea. This is a perception study with self-report outcomes only, which codebook section 3 sends to the screening report. Criteria 1, 2, and 3 'not_met' and core 'no' are right.

Counts are people: 25 students recruited from four Bavarian universities (PDF p. 4, Section 3.3), and 25 completed surveys and 25 transcribed interviews analyzed (p. 3, Section 3.1). This is below 50. Section 3.4 says incomplete submissions were discarded but gives no count, as the exclusions field says (p. 5).

participants.quote joins two verbatim sentences, from p. 4 Section 3.3 and p. 3 Section 3.1, in reverse page order. Programs, the semester range (5th Bachelor's to 3rd Master's), and lecturers from two German universities match (p. 4). 'six human educators' (abstract, p. 1) and 'five human professors, and one lecturer' (conclusion, p. 8) are verbatim.

Task and arms match: the task text, eight minutes of ideation plus a 15-minute refinement phase with an optional extension, and a 150-word critique form with three sections (p. 3). Figure 4 shows eight Crazy 8s ideas and one documented startup (p. 7). Comment A is the lecturer and comment B is GPT-4 (p. 5, Section 3.4, and p. 7, Figure 5).
S1-O1 reported: 'Positivity and supportiveness received median values 5.00 (p = 0.002, p < 0.05)' is verbatim (p. 5, H1). The Wilcoxon sentence is verbatim (p. 6, H5).

S1-O2 reported: the first quartile of 4.00, the medians of 4.00 and 5.00, and 'H2 was validated ... (p = 0.002, p < 0.05)' are verbatim (p. 6, H2). 'significant results (p < 0.05) across all sub-aspects' is verbatim (p. 7, H5).
S1-O3 reported: medians of 5.00 for correctness, context fit, and conclusiveness and p = 0.006 are verbatim (p. 6, H3).

Figure 3 panel titles are swapped, as the S1-O3 measure_detail says. The panel titled 'Coherence perception (H3)' shows structure, appearance, overview (time), spacing & paragraphing, and overall. The panel titled 'Structure and outer perception (H4)' shows correctness, context fit, conclusive, order, detail, and overall (p. 6).

Source caveat, not a form error: Figure 3 draws the AI medians for positiveness, supportiveness, correctness, context fit, and conclusive below 5, but the text gives 5.00. The form quotes the text correctly (p. 6).

Direction treatment_higher and statistics_available [p_value_only, figure_only] fit. The paper prints no test statistic, mean, or SD, and says students 'rated AI feedback markedly higher across all categories' (p. 7). H5 as stated covers H1, H2, and H4 (p. 4), but the results paragraph adds coherence, so the Wilcoxon result also applies to S1-O3 (p. 6).
One-line finding matches: 25 students, within-subjects, Wilcoxon p < 0.05 across all sub-aspects (p. 7), boxplots in Figure 3 (p. 6), and no creativity measure of the ideas (pp. 3-7).

H4 (structure, feedback generated in a median of 1.59 minutes, p = 0.001) and feedback duration are not listed as outcomes. The form-spec asks only for outcomes scored on output, so this is not a correction (p. 6).
summary: The form classifies c901 correctly: 25 students in a within-subjects design that randomized only the order in which they read GPT-4 and lecturer feedback on an idea they had already submitted, with self-reported perceptions of that feedback as the only outcomes, so there is no randomized people study and all three criteria fail. Every quoted statistic matches the PDF, but four wording fixes are needed: the paper never says the ideas were written without AI, states a 5-point scale only for the H1 and H4 items (Figure 3 plots every 'overall' item on 1 to 3), does not call the students design-related, and prints the Figure 1 sentence as an annotation, not the caption.
